compositionPlan.coldReadTarget: After a minute a newcomer can say what the page answers: Decide whether typed links improve answers about Brian's views across 30 chats enough to continue the linker work.
sketchInstructions: Put one short title at the top that states what this page answers and for whom.
Everything important is visible at once; no scrolling implied.
One main drawing occupies most of the area; other elements are visibly smaller and lighter.
Use at most three type sizes; headings heavier than body; important boxes larger.
Entry point top-left; the thing to do next bottom-right; if the order differs, number the parts.
Related items touch or nearly touch; unrelated items have clear gaps between them.
Every object of one kind is drawn the same way in every picture of the set.
Draw at most one level of boxes-around-groups; use white space for the rest.
Left edges of text and boxes line up on a few shared vertical lines.
Reuse one card style, one label style, and one legend position across the set.
Leave generous empty space around the main drawing and between groups.
No decorative borders, shadows, icons, or gridlines that carry no meaning.
Draw context in light grey and the subject in black.
Show the variants as a grid of identical small panels on one scale.
Any colour or badge used has its meaning shown right there.
A small status line shows source and date.
Exactly one kind of thing is highlighted; everything else is grey scale.
Draw each part in the form that fits its job: list, table, flow, or map.
Connections are lines or containment, not just items placed near each other.
Only draw a section or tab if the content shown needs it.
A stranger should get the point from the title and the main drawing alone.
Show a handful of objects at readable size, not dozens at tiny size.
